# cleura_openstack_project (Resource)

Manages an **OpenStack project** (a Keystone project, also called a tenant) in your Cleura
account. Projects are the unit that OpenStack resources, quotas, and user access are scoped
to: the `project_id` you give the Cleura provider, the OpenStack provider, or a Gardener
cluster refers to one of these.

Projects live in an **OpenStack domain**. A Cleura account normally has one domain per
region group, so by default the provider picks the domain that serves its configured
`region`. When that is ambiguous, set `domain_id` explicitly (list the candidates with
`cleura openstack domain list`).

`name`, `description`, and `enabled` are updated **in place**. `domain_id` cannot change
after creation; changing it creates a new project.

!> **Warning: creating a project is irreversible.** Cleura projects **cannot be deleted**, only
disabled — that is how Cleura works, not a provider limitation. The provider warns at plan time
when it is about to create one. `terraform destroy` **disables** the project (`enabled = false`),
removes it from Terraform state, and emits a warning; the disabled project — and any resources in
it — still exist in Cleura and still count toward your account's project quota. Re-enable it from
the Cleura Cloud control panel, or import it again with `enabled = true`.

For the same reason, changing `domain_id` — the one attribute that forces replacement — leaves you
with **two** projects: a new one in the new domain and the original, merely disabled, still holding
its name and quota slot. The provider warns about this at plan time. Prefer managing the project in
the other domain as a separate resource.

-> **Creating a project with `enabled = false`** takes two API calls, because the create endpoint
cannot set `enabled`: the project is created and then disabled. In the rare case where the second
call fails, the apply fails with the project already created and Terraform marks the resource
tainted. Do **not** re-run `apply` straight away — Terraform would try to replace the resource, and
the replacement cannot be created because the original still holds the name. Clear the taint and
apply again instead, which only disables the existing project:

```shell
terraform untaint cleura_openstack_project.example
terraform apply
```

The provider's error message says exactly this if you hit it.

~> **Note:** The Cleura API's project listing can lag behind a write by several minutes. A `plan`
run right after an `apply` may therefore show the change you just made as pending again; it
settles on its own. Re-applying is harmless.

~> **Note:** Reads use the list of projects the provider's API user can access. If that
user loses access to a managed project, the provider keeps the last known state and warns
instead of recreating the project.

-> **Domains:** the domain this resource lives in is derived from the provider's `region`; see
[OpenStack projects, users and domains](../guides/openstack-identity.md) for how that works and
when to set `domain_id`.

### Prerequisites

The provider must be authenticated and have a `region`. `project_id` is **not** required:
this resource is account-scoped. See the provider's
[Authentication](../index.md#authentication) documentation.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# An OpenStack project in the provider's region. The project is created in the
# OpenStack domain that serves that region; set domain_id to pick another one.
resource "cleura_openstack_project" "example" {
  name        = "team-sandbox"
  description = "Sandbox for the platform team"

  # Optional; defaults to true. Destroying the resource sets this to false,
  # because the Cleura API cannot delete projects.
  enabled = true
}

output "project_id" {
  value = cleura_openstack_project.example.id
}
```

## Import

```shell
# A project is imported by its OpenStack project ID (32 hex characters). Find it
# in the Cleura Cloud control panel, with `cleura openstack project list`, or
# with the cleura_openstack_project data source.
terraform import cleura_openstack_project.example 8a22c50af68e45c6b4dd7722cce8f93a
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Project name. Letters, digits, spaces, and `_ . - :` are allowed. Must be unique within the domain. Updated in place.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Free-text description. Removing it from the configuration clears it on the project. Updated in place. The API accepts only letters, numbers, spaces and the punctuation `. , _ : / -` — other characters are rejected at apply time.
- `domain_id` (String) OpenStack domain the project is created in. Defaults to the account's domain that serves the provider's `region` (or the account's only domain). Set it explicitly when the account has several domains for the region; list them with `cleura openstack domain list`. Changing it forces a new project.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the project is enabled. Defaults to `true`. A disabled project keeps its resources but cannot be used. Updated in place; destroying the resource sets this to `false`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) OpenStack project ID (32 hex characters), assigned by Cleura. Also the import ID.
